references.text: Moses cries out to the Lord in another crisis over water in the wilderness, showing a pattern of prayer in emergencies
A similar situation where the Lord gives water to the people in the wilderness at Meribah
Elisha heals the water at Jericho by throwing salt into it, paralleling how the tree was thrown into the water to make it sweet
The Lord tests the people with manna, just as he tested them at Marah with statutes and laws
The Lord tested Israel in the wilderness to know their heart, corresponding to the testing at Marah
Describes how God tested Israel in the wilderness, including the incident at Marah
Refers to how God tested Israel at the waters of Meribah, a parallel to the testing at Marah
Mentions how God gave water to his people in the wilderness
Encouragement to pray in suffering, as Moses cried out to the Lord in distress
Both verses deal with the people being put to the test (or putting God to the test) in connection with a lack of water.
Nehemiah summarizes and confirms God's provision of water during the wilderness journey, including the events at Marah.
